source_note: Written from the task text, tb_aes128_dec.sv, test_aes128_decrypt.py, FIPS 197 and the library model; RTL not read. Items marked AAn are in assumptions_arch.json.
byte_layout: 128-bit value: byte n = bits[127-8n : 120-8n]; state row = n%4, column = n//4; round key word j = bytes 4j..4j+3. Verified by the testbench vector (key 2b7e..., ct 3925..., pt 3243...).

interface.name: clk
interface.function: Clock; all registers change on the rising edge. TB period 10 time units (clk toggles every 5).

interface.name: rst_async_n
interface.timing: TB: low for 2 time units at start; cocotb: low for one clock, then high. Asserting it clears every register.
interface.function: Asynchronous active-low reset: idle, counters 0, key_done 0, state 0 so o_data = 0, o_done = 0 (AA6).

interface.name: i_update_key
interface.timing: level; only looked at in the row where i_start = 1; TB and cocotb drive it 0 in all later rows, so it must not be sampled again after the start row (AA10)
interface.function: 1 together with i_start: take i_key as the new cipher key, expand it first (10 clocks), then decrypt. 0 together with i_start: reuse the stored expanded key.

interface.name: i_key
interface.layout: byte 0 = bits[127:120] = first key byte (W[0] = bits[127:96]); FIPS 197 order
interface.timing: valid only in the start row (TB/cocotb set it to 0 right after); must be captured at the start edge when i_update_key = 1; ignored otherwise

interface.name: i_start
interface.timing: one-cycle pulse (TB: set at negedge, cleared at next negedge = sampled at exactly one rising edge; cocotb: one clock); sampled at the rising edge; ignored while busy (AA7)
interface.function: Starts one decryption of the block on i_data.

interface.name: i_data
interface.layout: byte n = bits[127-8n:120-8n] = state row n%4, column n//4 (TB comment: 39 25 84 1d is column 0)
interface.timing: valid only in the start row; TB/cocotb set it to 0 right after; must be latched at the start edge (AA8)

interface.name: o_done
interface.timing: 0 in the row after the start row (a stale 1 would make the cocotb loop compare too early); then 1 for exactly one row when o_data holds the plaintext; 0 again (AA4). The TB waits for a rising edge of o_done, so it must be 0 before the pulse.

interface.name: o_data
interface.timing: correct plaintext in the row where o_done = 1 (TB reads it at the negedge inside that row; cocotb reads it in the row it sees o_done = 1); after reset 0 (AA5, AA6); value in other rows not specified (AA5)

inputs.name: i_data
inputs.layout: byte 0 = MSB

outputs.name: state_in
outputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

timing.valid_when: always (captured into state_reg at the start edge)

blocks.function: Maps port i_data to the 4x4 state: byte n = i_data[127-8n -: 8], row n%4, column n//4. Pure wiring.

inputs.name: state_in
inputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

inputs.name: state_next
inputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

outputs.name: q
outputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

timing.valid_when: q holds: ciphertext after start edge; then result of the previous step; plaintext after round 11

blocks.function: 128-bit state. Loads i_data at the start edge (idle & i_start); holds during key expansion (key_cnt != 0); updates once per clock while round_cnt = 1..11; holds when idle. Reset 0.

inputs.name: rk0_in
inputs.layout: word j = bytes 4j..4j+3 = column j; word 0 = MSB

inputs.name: rk_next
inputs.layout: word j = bytes 4j..4j+3 = column j; word 0 = MSB

outputs.name: rk[0..10]
outputs.layout: word j = bytes 4j..4j+3 = column j; word 0 = MSB

timing.valid_when: rk[0] valid from the start edge of an update; rk[n] valid from the end of key step n; all 11 valid when key_done = 1

blocks.function: 11 x 128-bit expanded key, kept across operations (stored key reused when i_update_key = 0). rk[0] <= i_key at the start edge when i_update_key = 1; rk[n] <= next_round_key(rk[n-1], n) in key step n (n = 1..10).

inputs.name: prev_round_key
inputs.layout: word j = bytes 4j..4j+3 = column j; word 0 = MSB

outputs.name: next_round_key
outputs.layout: word j = bytes 4j..4j+3 = column j; word 0 = MSB

blocks.function: One step of the key schedule: round key n-1 -> n. t = Rcon(n) xor' SubWord(RotWord(w3)); w0' = w0^t; w1' = w1^w0'; w2' = w2^w1'; w3' = w3^w2'. (Equivalent to W[i] rules of the spec for i = 4n..4n+3.)

inputs.name: w3
inputs.layout: byte 0 = MSB

inputs.name: rot
inputs.layout: byte 0 = MSB

blocks.function: Apply the forward S-box to each byte (module sbox, already tested per the task text).

inputs.name: sub
inputs.layout: byte 0 = MSB

blocks.function: XOR Rcon[n] into byte 0 (the most significant byte) of the word. Rcon[1..10] = 01 02 04 08 10 20 40 80 1b 36 (already tested per the task text).

inputs.name: prev_round_key
inputs.layout: word j = bytes 4j..4j+3 = column j; word 0 = MSB

inputs.name: t
inputs.layout: byte 0 = MSB

outputs.name: next_round_key
outputs.layout: word j = bytes 4j..4j+3 = column j; word 0 = MSB

blocks.function: w0' = w0^t, w1' = w1^w0', w2' = w2^w1', w3' = w3^w2' (serial XOR chain across the four words).

outputs.name: round_key
outputs.layout: word j = bytes 4j..4j+3 = column j; word 0 = MSB

blocks.function: Decryption uses round keys in reverse: round_cnt 1 -> rk[10]; round_cnt r = 2..10 -> rk[11-r] (9..1); round_cnt 11 -> rk[0]. Note rounds 1..10 of the spec = round_cnt 2..11.

inputs.name: state
inputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

inputs.name: round_key
inputs.layout: word j = bytes 4j..4j+3 = column j; word 0 = MSB

outputs.name: state_out
outputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

blocks.function: Byte-wise XOR of state and round key (same byte layout).

inputs.name: state
inputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

outputs.name: state_out
outputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

blocks.function: Row r rotated right by r columns: out[r][c] = in[r][(c - r) mod 4]. Row 0 unchanged. Not used in round_cnt 1 (initial AddRoundKey).

inputs.name: state
inputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

outputs.name: state_out
outputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

blocks.function: Inverse S-box on each of the 16 bytes (module inv_sbox, already tested).

inputs.name: state
inputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

outputs.name: state_out
outputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

blocks.function: Each column multiplied by the circulant matrix [0E 0B 0D 09; 09 0E 0B 0D; 0D 09 0E 0B; 0B 0D 09 0E] in GF(2^8), polynomial 0x11B. Output after AddRoundKey (order InvShiftRows, InvSubBytes, AddRoundKey, InvMixColumns).

inputs.name: initial_path
inputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

inputs.name: round_path
inputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

inputs.name: final_path
inputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

outputs.name: state_next
outputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

blocks.function: Selects state_next: round_cnt 1 -> ARK(state, rk[10]) (no shift/sub/mix); round_cnt 2..10 -> InvMixColumns(ARK(InvSub(InvShift(state)), key)); round_cnt 11 -> ARK(InvSub(InvShift(state)), rk[0]) (no InvMixColumns).

inputs.name: q
inputs.layout: byte n = row n%4, col n//4; byte 0 = MSB

blocks.function: o_data = state_reg.q, byte n -> o_data[127-8n -: 8]. Inverse of load_block. No extra register (AA5).
0 = no key expansion running; start edge with i_update_key -> 1; counts 1..10 one per clock; after the clock with key_cnt = 10 returns to 0 and key_done becomes 1.
0 = idle; set to 1 at the start edge if no key update, or at the end of key step 10 if key update; counts 1..11 one per clock; returns to 0 after the clock with 11.
o_done <= 1 at the edge that ends round_cnt = 11, else 0. One-cycle pulse (AA4).
0 after reset and from the start edge of an update; 1 from the end of key step 10. Stays 1 across operations without update. Internal; not a port; the name is the architect's (AA12).

control.idle_definition: key_cnt = 0 and round_cnt = 0. A start is accepted only when idle (also in the row where o_done = 1) (AA7).

state_variables.key_cnt: 0, 1..10; step counter of the key expansion; value n = the clock in which round key n is computed and stored
state_variables.round_cnt: 0 idle, 1..11; value r = the clock in which step r of the table below is applied
state_variables.key_done: 1 when the stored expanded key is valid

events.name: reset
events.effect: key_cnt = round_cnt = 0; key_done = 0; o_done = 0; state_reg = 0; rk stores 0 (AA6)

events.name: start_with_update
events.effect: state_reg <= i_data; rk[0] <= i_key; key_done <= 0; key_cnt <= 1 (round_cnt stays 0)

events.name: key_step
events.effect: rk[n] <= next_round_key(rk[n-1], n); key_cnt <= n+1; state_reg holds

events.name: round_step
events.effect: state_reg <= step(r) per round_table; round_cnt <= r+1

events.name: round_last
events.effect: state_reg <= final round result; round_cnt <= 0; o_done <= 1 (for the next row only)

events.name: done_clear
events.effect: o_done <= 0 at the next edge (pulse); state_reg keeps the plaintext until the next start

control.update_flow: start row 0 -> rows 1..10 key_cnt = 1..10 (round keys 1..10) -> rows 11..21 round_cnt = 1..11 -> row 22 o_done = 1 with o_data = plaintext. All counts follow from AA1-AA3.
control.no_update_flow: start row 0 -> rows 1..11 round_cnt = 1..11 -> row 12 o_done = 1 with o_data = plaintext.
control.serial_rule: From the task text: the key expansion runs first, only then decryption steps start; decryption never overlaps with key steps. key_done = 1 is a precondition for round_cnt = 1.
control.o_done_rule: o_done = 1 only in the row after the clock with round_cnt = 11; never during key expansion (spec: not before the decryption is complete).

remember_across_cycles.why: TB and cocotb drive i_data = 0 from the row after start; the block must be latched at the start edge
i_key = 0 from the row after start; needed for all 10 key steps

remember_across_cycles.what: the decision 'update or not' (as key_cnt vs round_cnt, or an explicit flag)
remember_across_cycles.why: i_update_key = 0 in the rows after start (TB and cocotb clear it), so the flow cannot sample it again
a later start with i_update_key = 0 must reuse it; cocotb picks update_key at random per run
start is a one-cycle pulse and must not restart a running operation (AA7)

per_case.update: start_with_update, 10 x key_step, 11 x round_step, o_done

schedule.note: Row t = values seen during clock cycle t. Row 0 = the row in which i_start = 1 is presented (sampled at the edge that ends row 0). i_start/i_update_key show the inputs of that row. key_cnt/round/key_done/o_done are register values during the row. Spec-fixed: o_done = 0 in row 1 and 1 only when o_data is the plaintext (TB/cocotb). Everything else in the table depends on AA1-AA4 (row counts) and AA6 (key_done initial value).

fixed_by_spec: o_done at last row =1 with correct o_data
